info.description: Routes of OpenVibe.Watch as the OpenVibe contracts describe them (openvibe-contracts 0.235.0): each operation lists the capabilities it performs; a token for the service's audience must carry one of them unless the route is open. post.summary: Control a watch through OpenVibe.Watch's control API (ADR-048, plan T13 step 10): POST /api/v1/resources/control takes one common.resource-control-request@1 naming a watch.watch by its OVRN, from a fi
post.description: **watch.resource.control** (first-party): Control a watch through OpenVibe.Watch's control API (ADR-048, plan T13 step 10): POST /api/v1/resources/control takes one common.resource-control-request@1 naming a watch.watch by its OVRN, from a first-party service (OpenVibe.Services) acting for the person in on_behalf_of. Actions: suspend (pause the watch: nothing is checked until it resumes), resume (active again) and delete (remove it, as DELETE /api/v1/watches/:id); any other action is refused unsupported. Only the watch's owner may act on it, and only inside the project the OVRN names. dry_run decides and explains without applying. The first answer per (caller, project, idempotency_key) is kept and returned for a repeat; the same key with another request is refused. Answers common.resource-control-result@1.

common.resource-control-request.v1.title: ResourceControlRequest
common.resource-control-request.v1.description: common.resource-control-request@1: one control operation OpenVibe.Services (or Actor's Console) sends to the authority that owns a resource (ADR-048, plan T13). Services never mutates another service's database; every create, update, start, stop, delete, resize, rotate, pair, grant or revoke is this request to the owning authority's control API, which decides and answers with a common.resource-control-result@1. A request names exactly one of resource (every action but create) or resource_kind (create, before the name exists). project_id is the tenancy boundary and equals the project segment of resource. idempotency_key makes a retry safe: the authority answers a repeated key with the first result. A sensitive action (money, publishing, deleting, physical control) is refused with confirmation_required until its owner approves; the retry carries that confirmation_id (roadmap WS-Z2). The cross-field rules are checked by contracts.resources.checkControlRequest.

resource.description: The resource acted on; required for every action but create.

resource_kind.description: service.type (a common.resource-summary@1 kind), for create, before the resource name exists.

params.description: Action-specific input, shaped by the authority's own contract (never redefined here).

on_behalf_of.description: The subject whose grant the authority checks; the caller's own token says who sent it.

confirmation_id.description: The approved confirmation from an earlier confirmation_required answer.

common.resource-control-result.v1.title: ResourceControlResult
common.resource-control-result.v1.description: common.resource-control-result@1: the authority's answer to a common.resource-control-request@1 (ADR-048, plan T13). state is the outcome, not the resource's own state: done (applied), pending (accepted and asynchronous; the authority reports completion later on its events), refused (a policy or confirmation gate said no) or failed (an error). State rules: refused carries problem or confirmation_required; failed carries problem; done and pending carry neither; confirmation_required appears only on refused. result carries the authority's own response document and never another service's rows. The state rules are checked by contracts.resources.checkControlResult.

confirmation_required.description: The action needs its owner's approval; retry the same request with this confirmation_id once approved.

problem.description: RFC 9457 body when refused or failed.

common.resource-list-result.v1.title: ResourceListResult
common.resource-list-result.v1.description: A page of the resource index (roadmap WS-Z7).

partial.description: Authorities a merged index (OpenVibe.Services, ADR-048) could not read for this page: a slow or failing authority is omitted, never fails the page. Each entry names the authority and the problem code it answered. Added in 1.1.0; a single authority's own index leaves it out.

common.resource-name.v1.title: ResourceName
common.resource-name.v1.description: common.resource-name@1: the one stable, cross-service name of an OpenVibe resource (OVRN; ADR-034 section 2, ADR-048, plan T13): ovrn:<service>:<project_id>:<type>/<id>, for example ovrn:media:prj_01J0000000000000000000000A:object/med_01K0000000000000000000000B. The service segment is the authority that owns the resource; the project segment is its tenancy boundary; type is the second half of a common.resource-summary@1 kind and id is that summary's id, so the name composes from any resource summary. It is used in grant scopes, audit rows, event subjects, usage records, bill lines and console URLs. It never names a person, an app, a request, a session or an event. The pattern is the one common.usage-recorded@1 resource and common.resource-summary@1 ovrn already use.

common.resource-summary.v1.title: ResourceSummary
common.resource-summary.v1.description: One resource of any service, as the resource index lists it (roadmap WS-Z7): every service answers GET /api/v1/resources with these, so OpenVibe.Services shows any resource without owning its data.

kind.description: service.kind, e.g. watch.watch, actor.actor, media.object, events.subscription

ovrn.description: Optional resource name (ADR-034 section 2), the name grants, audit, events, usage records and bills use: ovrn:<service>:<project_id>:<type>/<id>, e.g. ovrn:watch:<project_id>:watch/<wch_id>, with the pattern of common.usage-recorded@1 resource. Its service, project and id are this summary's service, project_id and id. Added in 1.1.0.

errors.problem.v1.title: Problem
errors.problem.v1.description: RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) with a stable OpenVibe error code and trace identifiers. The legacy 'error' string is allowed during migration so existing clients keep working.

error.description: Deprecated compatibility field: same text as title/detail for clients that read {error}.

identity.subject-ref.v1.title: SubjectRef
identity.subject-ref.v1.description: The one cross-platform reference to an actor. Issued by OpenVibe.Network. Never a service-local integer id.

oneOf.description: AgentSubject: an agent (OpenVibe.Actor, or a developer app's agent) acting under grants its owner delegated (roadmap WS-Z2). In an event envelope, on_behalf_of names the owner.

platform.runtime-class.v1.title: RuntimeClass
platform.runtime-class.v1.description: platform.runtime-class@1: the kind of execution environment a platform.job@1 asks for (plan T14 Run; ADR-034 proposed). A name only: this contract defines no behavior, and a worker runs only the classes it advertises and refuses every other one (`nack`). `function` is the first class implemented (OpenVibe.Node's function worker); the others are reserved names. Each class names one reserved Fabric capability in platform.resource-offer@1.capabilities — `worker:` + the class (worker:function, worker:code, worker:browser, worker:linux, worker:desktop, worker:gpu) — and a node advertises the name of each class it runs.
platform.runtime-class.v1.$comment: Additive: a class may be added to v1; none is removed, renamed or reordered.

oneOf.description: A pre-registered artifact (name and exact version) run once with declared args to one result: single-shot, no persistent filesystem, no dependency resolution, network denied.
Arbitrary source with its dependency tree in a longer-lived environment; needs image handling and isolation stronger than a container.
A headless or headed web browser session driven remotely.
A full Linux environment (shell, filesystem, processes) that lives across commands.
A graphical desktop session with screen and input under control levels.
A workload that holds one or more GPUs for its lifetime.

platform.workload-requirements.v1.title: WorkloadRequirements
platform.workload-requirements.v1.description: What a workload needs, so the platform can place it (roadmap WS-Z9). Hard constraints are filtered before any objective is scored; a cheaper candidate that misses one is never chosen.

kind.description: what runs, e.g. watch.browser, media.transcode, ai.run, events.deliver

residency.description: region or jurisdiction the work and its data must stay in

trust.description: trust classes allowed to run it (ADR-046); when absent, first-party, partner, community and external. user-owned is never a default: a user-owned offer is eligible only when this list names it

partition_key.description: stable key for rendezvous placement (room, stream, session)

run.job-create-request.v1.title: RunJobCreateRequest
run.job-create-request.v1.description: run.job-create-request@1 (PLANNED; plan T14 R1, ADR-034): the body of POST /api/v1/jobs on OpenVibe.Run (capability run.job.submit). The job belongs to the project the caller's token names, or, for a first-party service acting for a person (X-OV-Subject), the project it names with X-OV-Project once Network confirms the person is an admin or owner of it (ADR-003 amendment 2026-10-12); the person is then the requester and the service is recorded as via. CLASS is a platform.runtime-class@1 name; Run accepts any of them but places a job only on a node that advertises worker:<class> (platform.resource-offer@1), so a class no node runs today (browser, linux, desktop, gpu) ends expired with run.job.unplaceable. ARTIFACT is the pre-registered artifact to run (name and one exact version), required for function and code, as platform.job@1 carries it. ARGS is the artifact's declared input as JSON (at most 512 KiB serialized, else 413). INPUTS are files placed in the job directory before the process starts, each an OpenVibe.Media object pinned by its sha256: a size or digest mismatch fails the job (run.job.input_digest_mismatch) before the process ever runs; Run never fetches a caller-chosen URL. LIMITS are hard caps merged stricter with the node's own (platform.job@1 limits); a request over the project's tier cap is refused 422 run.limits.exceeded, never silently lowered. EGRESS is the network the job may reach, the values of OpenVibe.Node's worker.egress, carried per job as the same-named platform.job@1 net: none (default; no network), public or openvibe-only. A job asking for public or openvibe-only is placed only on a node whose worker.egress allows it; a worker whose host policy is stricter runs the stricter one. REQUIREMENTS (platform.workload-requirements@1) narrow placement; absent means { kind: run.<class>, mobility: job, latency_class: background, objective: balanced }. IDEMPOTENCY_KEY: a repeat from the same project within 24 h with an identical body answers the first job (200, created false); with a different body 409 run.idempotency.conflict.

args.description: The artifact's declared input as JSON; default {}.

inputs.description: Files placed in the job directory before the process starts; names are unique (else 422).

ttl_ms.description: Lifetime from creation, covering the wait for a node and the run (platform.job@1 ttl_ms); when it runs out the job ends expired. Default: limits.wall_ms plus 600000.

artifact.description: The pre-registered artifact to run (platform.job@1 artifact).

version.description: One exact version, never a range

input.description: One input file: an OpenVibe.Media object the caller's project can read, pinned by digest.

name.description: File name in the job directory; no path separators.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the object's bytes.

limits.description: Caps on the running process (platform.job@1 limits); hitting one ends the job failed with run.job.limit.

egress.description: OpenVibe.Node worker.egress values: none (no network), public (the internet without private, link-local or the network's own ranges), openvibe-only (the network's own endpoints only).

watch.check-run.v1.title: WatchCheckRun
watch.check-run.v1.description: watch.check-run@1: one execution of a watch's check (plan T18), by schedule, manually, or from a delivered event or webhook. carrier names the mechanism that carried it; state is the terminal state (the same values the service's check_runs.state CHECK allows). observations is how many observations the run recorded and triggers how many conditions it fired; cost_usd is what the run cost. Rows are immutable.

watch.observation.v1.title: WatchObservation
watch.observation.v1.description: watch.observation@1: one value a check recorded for a watch (plan T18): what was extracted, when, from which check run, and whether it changed or met the condition. value is the extracted value exactly as the source stated it, never inferred; snapshot is a capped copy of the raw body kept according to the watch's retention. Rows are immutable.

value.description: The extracted value as the source stated it: text, a decimal number, a structured object.

value_hash.description: SHA-256 hex of the canonical value.

previous_hash.description: SHA-256 of the previous observation's value; null for the first observation.

watch.watch-request.v1.title: WatchRequest
watch.watch-request.v1.description: watch.watch-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/watches and PATCH /api/v1/watches/:id on OpenVibe.Watch (watch.watch.manage; the acting person). Every field is optional on a patch, project_id included (null clears it); a create requires source, extraction, condition and action, which the service enforces in code (422 watch.invalid).

project_id.description: The project the watch's project work belongs to (its run-job actions are billed to it). The acting person must be an admin or owner of the unarchived project: Watch checks with Network when it is saved (network.project.member.read; 403 project.not_delegated otherwise) and OpenVibe.Run checks again at every job (ADR-003 amendment 2026-10-12). null clears it.

project_env.description: The project environment the watch's project secrets (ADR-056: a source credential's or a webhook action's secret_ref) are looked up in. Defaults to production when the watch names a project; meaningless without one.

watch.watch-result.v1.title: WatchResult
watch.watch-result.v1.description: watch.watch-result@1: answers of the watch routes on OpenVibe.Watch. GET /api/v1/watches → { watches } and POST /api/v1/watches → 201 { watch } (watch.watch.read, watch.watch.manage); PATCH → { watch }; POST /:id/pause and /:id/resume → { id, status }; DELETE /api/v1/watches/:id → { id, deleted: true }.

watch.watch.v1.title: Watch
watch.watch.v1.description: watch.watch@1: a user-defined persistent observation (plan T18). It names a source (a push event, a webhook, a conditional HTTP URL, a feed or API, a local Node probe, or an expensive Run check), how a value is extracted, how it is compared with the last observation, the condition that fires, the actions it wakes, its budget and its retention. Carrier preference is binding: an event or webhook source is used when one exists, then ETag/Last-Modified, then a feed, then an API, and browser polling through Run only when none works. A price or stock is 'as of' the observation, null when it stated none.

project_env.description: The project environment its project secrets (ADR-056, secret_ref) are looked up in; null when the watch names no project.

owner.description: The acting person or agent the watch belongs to: usr_…, agt_… or svc:….

env.description: The name of the environment variable holding the credential; Watch reads it by name at fetch time and never stores the value.

secret_ref.description: Instead of env: the name of a project secret (ADR-056) in the watch's project and project_env, granted to watch for reveal to the source URL's origin. OpenVibe.Network answers the value at fetch time; Watch never stores it.

conditional.description: Send If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since from the stored ETag/Last-Modified when the server gave one.

node_id.description: The machine (an OpenVibe.Bot device id, dev_…) the check runs from: the owner's own, with "Let my watches check things from this computer" on.

probe.description: { target, timeout_s }: bot.command@1's probe value. target is http(s)://… (one GET from the machine; the answer's body is the document) or tcp://host:port (the document is { open, ms }).

cadence.description: Required for http/feed/api/node sources; null for event/webhook sources (they never poll).

secret_ref.description: Instead of secret_env: the name of a project secret (ADR-056) in the watch's project and project_env, granted to watch for sign. OpenVibe.Network signs each delivery in the same headers; Watch never holds the value.

oneOf.description: Run one of the watch owner's personal agents on OpenVibe.Actor (actor.agent.run, Actor 0.140.0 contracts): the firing is the run's input, after the optional note. The agent must belong to the watch's owner; its own budgets and daily cap apply.

args.description: The artifact's declared input as JSON; default {}.

firing_arg.description: The args key the firing is added under; null or absent: none.

oneOf.description: Start one OpenVibe.Run job when the watch fires (run.job-create-request@1 fields). The job is billed to the watch's project_id, which the watch must name; Watch starts it as itself acting for the owner (X-OV-Subject) in that project (X-OV-Project, ADR-003 amendment 2026-10-12), so Run checks the owner is an admin or owner of the project and applies the project's tier caps. CLASS and LIMITS are required, and ARTIFACT for function and code (Watch refuses a watch without them, 422 watch.invalid). FIRING_ARG names the args key the firing (watch id, check run, value, previous value, observed_at) is added under; without it the job gets ARGS as written. The idempotency key watch.<check run>.<action index> makes a retried delivery the same job. RUNTIME, COMMAND and WORKLOAD are the field names of an earlier draft that never ran: they are not accepted (422 watch.invalid).

openvibeToken.description: An OpenVibe Network token for this service: a person's token, an app token (client credentials, audience of the service) or a first-party service token. Its `cap` claim must include the capability the operation names.
